evidence.quote: This is attributted to the fact that dislocations on γ'/γ interfaces help to relax the local misﬁt strains, causing some to expand at the expense of others.

This is at- tributed to the effect of dislocations in relaxing the lattice mis ﬁt, resulting in net mis ﬁt anisotropy, elastic strain anisotropy and in turn elastic stain energy anisotropy.

Screw dislocations can easily change gliding direction via cross-slip and have the better ability to navigate through the narrow γ channels
The selective migration of elements from one location to other results in the conversion of γ' to γ at one location and γ to γ’ at another, thus rafting.
The anisotropic dislocation structures at theγ'/γ interfaces are effec- tive in causing anisotropic rafting of the γ' phase cuboids.

conflicts.topic: rafting driving force: elastic strain energy / hydrostatic stress anisotropy vs anisotropic dislocation structure
claims: Elastic strain energy and hydrostatic stress anisotropies are ruled out to be responsible for rafting.
An anisotropic dislocation structure on the {001} γ'/γ interfaces is a direct cause of rafting.

evidence.quote: The elastic strain energy and hydrostatic stress anisotropies are ruled out to be responsible for rafting.

conflicts.topic: validity of Elastic Model as rafting mechanism
conflicts.description: The Elastic Model predicts elastic strain energy anisotropies whose predicted raft structure contradicts experimental observations, yet the study still supports misfit elastic strain energy anisotropy as a driving force for rafting.

evidence.quote: this study disquali ﬁes the Elastic Model as an effective mechanism for rafting, but does not dispose the validity of elastic stain energy anisot- ropy as a driving force for rafting.
